title: a host-module edge in a parameter default is part of the pinned function's graph
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin': the assertion is over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE GRAPH, so a requirement reached through another module is the same requirement, and 'The diagnostic SHOULD show the dependency path that introduced the requirement.' `Module<"node:fs">` is poc/src/targets/classify.ts's concrete spelling of the JavaScript-host dependence that page names, and `blocksNativePin` refuses `TypeScript`, `Module<...>` and `Host<...>` together. `messageContains` pins the route because a pin refused with an empty route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly. The SMITHERS1510 companion lands in the auxiliary module, at the edge that reaches `node:fs`, because a re-export runs the target module's initializer exactly as an import does; it is declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract (conformance/README.md). No laundering module here: the `node:fs` import is on line 2 of the case itself. What hides the edge is the POSITION of the reference — a default expression, which executes inside `pinned` on every call that omits the argument, and which a body-only walk never visits. Both backends refuse it today, so this case pins current behaviour on both rather than reproducing a live one-sided defect; the historical defect is the reference's, and it could not be reproduced here because reverting poc/src/targets/classify.ts is another lane's work.
